sections.html:
A Walker owner can work with an agent, search for a buyer alone, or sell to a cash buyer who accepts the property as is. The city sits in Kent County beside Grand Rapids, so its market moves with the larger metro area.

Timing and condition pick the route. A tidy house with weeks to spare usually fares best on the open market. Deferred repairs, a tenant or an estate can make a buyer without a lender appraisal the easier match.

  • Agent: more exposure and a likelier top price, against a commission and a longer path to closing.
  • Alone: no commission, though contract, disclosures and deed fall to you.
  • Cash: fewer conditions and a set closing date, typically at a lower price than a polished listing.

Put every offer in writing, including who pays transfer tax and title costs.

Walker incorporated as a city in 1962, which kept Grand Rapids from annexing it. It has 25,881 residents as of 2025, up 2.9% from the 2020 base, and covers 24.58 square miles. I-96 forms the northern side, US 131 touches the northeast, Alpine Avenue (M-37) joins the interstate, and Lake Michigan Drive (M-45) cuts across the center. Meijer and Bissell are both headquartered here.

Homes carry a median value of $295,200. Owners live in 65.2% of homes, so many Walker units are rentals. The 20.2-minute average commute is short, and buyers working along I-96 or downtown value that access.

Four public school districts serve the city: Comstock Park Public Schools, Grand Rapids Public Schools, Grandville Public Schools and Kenowa Hills Public Schools. Kenowa Hills runs Central Elementary and Zinser Elementary inside the city and zones its middle and high school students to buildings in Alpine Township. Cummings Elementary, from Grandville, and Walker Charter Academy are also in the city limits.

Covenant Christian High School and Hope Protestant Reformed Christian School are private options in Walker, and the Kent District Library has a Walker branch.

Four districts share one small city, so the district for a house can change from one block to the next. Name the district in the listing and ask Walker's assessor to confirm it for your parcel.

sections.h2: Walker tax bills and the city income tax
sections.html:
Walker's summer bill goes out July 1 and is due September 14, and the winter bill goes out December 1 and is due February 14. Summer carries over 90% of the year's tax. Payment must arrive by 5 p.m. on the due date, and a postmark does not count.

  • Late summer payments: 1% interest begins September 15, 4% more October 1, then 1% each month from November to February.
  • Late winter payments: a 3% penalty begins February 15.
  • Real property taxes still open on March 1 pass to the Kent County Treasurer.

Each bill includes a 1% administration fee. A principal residence earns relief from 18 school operating mills when the owner lives there on May 1 and has filed the exemption affidavit with Walker's assessor. After a sale, Michigan law resets the buyer's taxable value in the calendar year following the transfer.

The city also taxes income, 1% for residents and one-half of 1% for non-residents, through its Income Tax Department at 616-791-6880. Ask the income tax office whether any gain from your sale is reportable on the city return. The treasurer is open Monday through Thursday until 5 p.m. and Friday until 11:30 a.m.

No rental certification program exists in Walker. Each property must instead meet the 2021 International Property Maintenance Code as amended in City Code Section 18-90, and staff act on complaints rather than patrolling.

The city lists the usual complaints, with their code sections, so a seller can check a house before listing:

  • Accumulations of junk and inoperable vehicles, under Section 50-142.
  • Tall grass and noxious weeds, under Section 90-3.
  • Fences, accessory structures, and parking on the lawn, under Chapter 94.
  • Recreational vehicle and trailer storage.
  • Sidewalk snow removal, under Section 70-68.

Code Enforcement can be reached at (616) 735-6129. Building inspections and plan review are contracted to Professional Code Inspections, and permits can be applied for through the BS&A portal or on paper. A certificate of occupancy is issued after the final inspections and zoning items are approved. The Community Development office at 4243 Remembrance Rd. NW takes calls at 616-791-6858.

The city runs its records through the BS&A Online portal. A visitor can search assessing records, view property sale data, look up current taxes, find permit and inspection history, and see the registered rental properties in the municipality. Searches work by address, owner name or parcel number.

The same portal handles building permit applications and inspection scheduling. The city publishes separate guides for new construction, remodels, pools and spas, accessory buildings and decks, and a Kent County Health Department environmental review form is part of the packet where it applies. A buyer who sees an unpermitted deck or finished basement in the inspection can use these guides to learn what the city would require.

Most questions about permits and zoning go to staff at the Community Development office.

Before you list, search your own parcel in the portal. You can see your tax status, your permit history and any inspection records, and you can hand a buyer the same information. Gathering it early means fewer surprises when a buyer's inspector asks about a deck, a finished basement or an older permit.

sections.h2: Recording a Walker deed in Kent County
sections.html:
Deeds for Walker properties go to the Kent County Register of Deeds in the County Administration Building at 300 Monroe Avenue NW in Grand Rapids. The office does not supply blank deeds or give advice on preparing them, so a title company or a Michigan real property attorney usually drafts the document.

Transfer tax is based on the consideration paid. The state rate is $3.75 for each $500 of value (MCL 207.525), the seller is liable (MCL 207.523), and the county rate is set by MCL 207.504 at 55 cents per $500 in a county of under 2,000,000 people. Ask the Register of Deeds for the current county amount and the recording fee, because fee schedules change.

Exempt transfers need a citation to MCL 207.526 on the deed, including family conveyances to a child or grandchild and foreclosure transfers.

faqs.a: No. Walker is its own Kent County city, formed in 1962. Many addresses carry Grand Rapids ZIP code names for mail.

faqs.q: Must a Walker rental be certified before I sell it?
faqs.a: Not by the city. Walker has no rental certification program, but the 2021 property maintenance code applies and enforcement follows complaints.

faqs.q: What dates matter for Walker property taxes?
faqs.a: Due dates are September 14 for the summer bill and February 14 for the winter bill, by 5 p.m. Unpaid real property tax goes to the Kent County Treasurer on March 1.

faqs.q: Does Walker have a city income tax?
faqs.a: Yes: 1% for residents and one-half of 1% for non-residents, handled by the Walker Income Tax Department.
For 2020 through 2024, owner-occupied homes had a median value of $295,200 and median rent was $1,202.
